newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end up higher on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end up higher on technical buying.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed higher as speculators and locals took profits in a technical correction to Wednesday's losses, market sources said.
"We made new lows yesterday, attempted to stabilize and saw a bit of short covering today," said Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter.

Wednesday, prices fell to four-year lows after USDA kept the Florida crop at a record 220 million 90-lb boxes. Belying market expectations, USDA increased yields to 1.54 gallons a box from 1.53 gallons.
Analysts warned that the fundamental outlook remains negative, however. High retail prices have dampened demand for orange juice while abundant supplies are projected for Brazil.
Temperatures across Florida's citrus belt will drop this weekend but are not expected to dip low enough to threaten the crop, forecasters said.
Technically, the market will turn its attention to rolling March positions into May, traders said. The first notice day for the spot month is March 3.
The March/May spread closed at a 3.15 cent discount.
March closed 2.35 cents higher at 76.90 cents a pound after trading from 77.40 to 74.55. The back months settled 1.95 to 1.85 higher.
Support was pegged between 67.00 and 66.00 cents in March.
Volume was estimated at 7,000 lots compared with Wednesday's official volume of 7,047 lots. ((Suzanne Rostler, New York Commodities Desk 212-859-1646))
